claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain relative to commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced toughness relative to commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
The proposed enhancement in plastic strain and toughness is governed by multicomponent-induced lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion promotes more homogeneous dislocation mobility in WTaTiVZr.
Lattice distortion facilitates grain-boundary sliding in WTaTiVZr.
Homogeneous dislocation mobility and grain-boundary sliding delay crack nucleation and propagation.
Atomic-size differences among W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr produce lattice-distortion fields and alter grain-boundary structure.
Atomic-size misfit and varying bonding interactions in equimolar WTaTiVZr create pervasive lattice distortions.
The lattice distortions lower the barrier for dislocation motion across multiple slip systems.
Distributed plastic deformation caused by dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding increases the alloy's toughness relative to pure tungsten.
Matched WTaTiVZr and pure-tungsten specimens should be tested under identical high-temperature tensile and creep conditions to isolate the proposed compositional lattice-distortion effect.
WTaTiVZr is predicted to exhibit a higher strain to failure than pure tungsten at 1000–1500 °C.
WTaTiVZr is predicted to exhibit greater toughness, measured as a larger area under the stress–strain curve, than pure tungsten at 1000–1500 °C.
WTaTiVZr is predicted to exhibit more uniform and spatially distributed plastic deformation than pure tungsten.
The proposed effect is expected only where thermally activated dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding are significant and no phase change or surface degradation occurs.
The mechanism of lattice distortion promoting enhanced dislocation mobility is well established theoretically.
The magnitude of any WTaTiVZr improvement over pure tungsten and the contributions of individual elements remain uncertain.

Comparable or superior plasticity and toughness in matched pure tungsten, or failure of WTaTiVZr by mechanisms inconsistent with enhanced dislocation mobility and grain-boundary sliding, would falsify the hypothesis.
